summary_paraphrase: Two competitive friends play football; the small millipede beats the hen five to one, the hen swallows him in a rage, his mother tells him to use his foul taste, he is coughed out, and the tale ends by explaining why chickens and millipedes are enemies.

characters.name: Millipede
characters.change: from friend to enemy of chickens
characters.humor_source: tiny but wins five goals; laughs at the fuss

characters.name: Mother Millipede
characters.relation_to_protagonist: mother; tells him how to save himself

humor_notes: Size reversal (tiny millipede outplays the hen), the five ways of scoring, the burp-spit-sneeze-cough sequence.

repetition.description: 'X was …, but Millipede was …-er' comparisons, then three ways of scoring
repetition.why: each line escalates Chicken's humiliation and builds toward the outburst

repetition.description: burp, swallow, spit, sneeze, cough, cough
repetition.why: a read-aloud list that turns the danger into slapstick

notes: The size gap between hen and millipede is carried by the pictures and makes the result funny.
The scoreboard (1 and 5) sits beside the swallowing scene, tying the act to the score.
Close-ups of Chicken's face mark her rising anger (p5) and her sickness (p9).

strengths: clear escalation from competition to rage
the small character's own trait (foul taste) is the escape
strong read-aloud sound sequence on page 10
weaknesses: the friendship breaks and is never repaired
the protagonist is saved on his mother's instruction
aggression toward a friend is the climax

anti_patterns.note: Mother tells Millipede what to do; he only follows
for a friendship reading the ending answers 'why are they enemies', not the friends' conflict; as a pourquoi tale it is complete

child_appeal_heuristic.rationale: Scores are the analyst's reading of the pages, not observations of children.
child_appeal_heuristic.label: Research heuristic — not validated

age_suitability.notes: A friend swallows a friend in anger and the friendship ends in permanent enmity: research intensity 5/5 at p6, above the engine's 0-3 ceiling for 5-6 (would be 3+). Useful only as structure (competition escalation, pourquoi ending).

metrics.lexicon_note: direct_address and sound_words are lexicon counts: a floor, not a measure. direct_address counts second-person words anywhere, dialogue included — it is not narrator-to-reader address

repetition.end_rhyme_note: heuristic: consecutive lines sharing a final two letters
